title: CS-01 First Response Time: declared formula, numerator and denominator with honest missing-data behaviour
risk: The First Response Time figure is produced under different accounting rules - the mean published as the median with no p95, so the slower half of the customer base is invisible - so the KPI is wrong in the direction that flatters the programme and every decision taken on it inherits the error.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
Metric scope is fixed before measurement: numerator is first-response intervals measured end to end on the message timestamps; denominator is conversations with a value-bearing first reply.
The dictionary entry for 'First Response Time' (owner, unit, window, exclusion rule) is loaded read-only and is compared with the recomputation instead of being trusted.

inputs.formula: median and p95 seconds between the first customer message and the first value-bearing reply
inputs.wrong_value_if_buggy: the mean published as the median with no p95, so the slower half of the customer base is invisible
inputs.expected_boundary_behaviour: a conversation with no value-bearing reply is unresolved and excluded from the percentile sample, never counted as 0 seconds

steps.action: Compute First Response Time from the frozen rows in kpi_dataset.care
steps.expected: The stored aggregate reports median 2.5s and p95 4s and records the formula, the window and the currency that produced it.

steps.action: Recompute First Response Time independently from the raw counter rows for the same tenant and window
steps.expected: The recomputed value equals the stored value median 2.5s and p95 4s, and every numerator row lies inside the denominator scope.

steps.action: Force the empty-source variant of the metric (no qualifying row in the window)
steps.expected: The metric reports a conversation with no value-bearing reply is unresolved and excluded from the percentile sample, never counted as 0 seconds; the display distinguishes missing source data from a measured zero.

steps.action: Read the dashboard payload and the metric dictionary entry
steps.expected: The dashboard renders the stored value with its window, coverage and source, and the dictionary names the owner, unit, numerator and denominator that the recomputation used.

assertions: First Response Time equals median 2.5s and p95 4s for the frozen window, recomputed from the raw counter rows with numerator scope 'first-response intervals measured end to end on the message timestamps' and denominator scope 'conversations with a value-bearing first reply'.

A recomputation that yields the mean published as the median with no p95, so the slower half of the customer base is invisible is detected as wrong: the stored aggregate and the independent recomputation must agree before the figure is published.
The dashboard payload for the same tenant and window carries the stored value with its window, coverage and measurement source; it substitutes neither a design target nor another metric's value.

Boundary behaviour: a conversation with no value-bearing reply is unresolved and excluded from the percentile sample, never counted as 0 seconds; missing source data is never rendered as a measured zero.
forbidden: Counting an automatic acknowledgement as a first response.
Publishing the median while the required p95 is omitted.
evidence: Percentile computation sheet with the sample size.
cleanup: Delete gov- aggregate, raw-counter and scenario rows for CS-01 after exporting the recomputation table.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
